lines.rookie: A light burned at the list desk from eleven until one. Thin paper showed the list was copied. Mr. Nam Giho, a new clerk, left last. Haesu, a keeper, saw the first clue. The Provisional Government began in Shanghai in April 1919, and Kim Gu was its police chief. His police guarded it and watched for spies. Later, in 1940, Kim Gu became its head.
lines.junior: A light burned at the list desk from eleven until one. Thin paper showed that the list had been copied. Mr. Nam Giho, a new clerk, was the last to leave. Haesu, a keeper, noticed the first clue. The Provisional Government began in Shanghai in April 1919, and Kim Gu was its police chief. His police protected it and watched for spies. Later, in 1940, Kim Gu became the head of the government.
lines.master: A light burned at the list desk from eleven until one, and thin paper proved the list had been copied. Mr. Nam Giho, a newly arrived clerk, was the last to leave. Haesu, one of the keepers, spotted the first clue. The Provisional Government was founded in Shanghai in April 1919, with Kim Gu as its police chief; his police guarded it and kept watch for spies. Later, in 1940, Kim Gu rose to become its head.

lines.rookie: Then let me show you what happened, Chief Kim.
lines.junior: Then let me show you what really happened, Chief Kim.
lines.master: Then allow me to show you what took place, Chief Kim.

lines.rookie: When did this government begin?
lines.junior: When did this government start?
lines.master: When was this government founded?

lines.rookie: In April 1919, here in Shanghai.
lines.junior: In April 1919, right here in Shanghai.
lines.master: In April 1919, here in Shanghai itself.

lines.rookie: It began after the March First Movement at home.
lines.junior: It started after the March First Movement back home.
lines.master: It was born after the March First Movement at home.

lines.rookie: What is your work here?
lines.junior: What do you do here?
lines.master: What is your role here?

lines.rookie: I became the police chief in August 1919.
lines.junior: In August 1919, I became the police chief.
lines.master: I was made police chief in August 1919.

lines.rookie: I asked only to guard the door. They gave me more.
lines.junior: I only asked to guard the door, but they gave me more.
lines.master: All I asked was to guard the door. They gave me far more.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "When was someone at my list desk?"
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "When was somebody at my list desk?"
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "At what hours was someone at my list desk?"

lines.rookie: From eleven until one. Half of a new candle burned.
lines.junior: From eleven until one. Half of a new candle burned away.
lines.master: From eleven until one. Half of a new candle was consumed.

lines.rookie: Two hours with our list. That is long.
lines.junior: Two hours with our list. That is a long time.
lines.master: Two whole hours with our list. That is a long while.

lines.rookie: That does not show when.
lines.junior: That doesn't show when.
lines.master: That says nothing of when.

lines.rookie: Haesu's note tells when the light burned.
lines.junior: Haesu's note tells you when the light burned.
lines.master: Haesu's note reveals when the light burned.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "How do you know the list was copied?"
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "How can you tell the list was copied?"
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "What tells you the list was copied?"

lines.rookie: Your report found thin paper with names pressed into it.
lines.junior: Your own report found thin paper with names pressed into it.
lines.master: The thin paper your report found has names pressed into it.

lines.rookie: He wrote over the list. An old trick.
lines.junior: He wrote over the list. That is an old trick.
lines.master: He traced over the list. An old trick indeed.

lines.rookie: That does not show copying.
lines.junior: That doesn't show copying.
lines.master: That proves no copying.

lines.rookie: The police report found the thin paper.
lines.junior: The police report is where the thin paper was found.
lines.master: It was the police report that found the thin paper.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "Who was here when the light went out?"
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "Who was still here when the light went out?"
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "Who remained here when the light went out?"

lines.rookie: Mr. Nam Giho. He signed out at a quarter past one.
lines.junior: Mr. Nam Giho. He signed the book at a quarter past one.
lines.master: Mr. Nam Giho. He signed himself out at a quarter past one.

lines.rookie: The new clerk. He was asking too many questions.
lines.junior: The new clerk. He asked far too many questions.
lines.master: The new clerk. He was always asking too many questions.

lines.rookie: That does not show who.
lines.junior: That doesn't show who.
lines.master: That says nothing of who.

lines.rookie: The sign-out book shows who left last.
lines.junior: The sign-out book shows who was the last to leave.
lines.master: The sign-out book reveals who left last.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu asks: "Why does our government need police, so far from home?"
lines.junior: Kim Gu asks: "Then why does a government in exile need police?"
lines.master: Kim Gu asks: "So what need has a government in exile for police?"

lines.rookie: Your police guard the government and watch for spies.
lines.junior: Your police are there to guard the government and watch for spies.
lines.master: Your police guard the government and keep watch for spies.

lines.rookie: Yes. Far from home, our government must be kept safe.
lines.junior: Yes. So far from home, our government has to be kept safe.
lines.master: Indeed. So far from home, our government must be kept safe.

lines.rookie: That does not say what the police do.
lines.junior: That doesn't say what the police do.
lines.master: That does not describe the work of the police.

lines.rookie: The police report says what Kim Gu's police do.
lines.junior: The police report tells what Kim Gu's police do.
lines.master: The police report describes the work of Kim Gu's police.

lines.rookie: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.junior: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.master: CLOSE THE CASE

lines.rookie: By noon, Mr. Nam Giho has left Shanghai. The real list is safe.
lines.junior: By noon, Mr. Nam Giho has gone from Shanghai. The real list is safe.
lines.master: By noon, Mr. Nam Giho has vanished from Shanghai, and the real list is safe.

lines.rookie: I only counted a candle, sir.
lines.junior: All I did was count a candle, sir.
lines.master: I merely counted a candle, sir.

lines.rookie: Small things keep big things safe, Haesu.
lines.junior: Little things keep big things safe, Haesu.
lines.master: It is the small things that keep the big things safe, Haesu.

lines.rookie: Korea's Provisional Government began in Shanghai in April 1919.
lines.junior: In April 1919, Korea's Provisional Government began in Shanghai.
lines.master: Korea's Provisional Government was founded in Shanghai in April 1919.

lines.rookie: Kim Gu was its police chief. His police guarded it and watched for spies.
lines.junior: Kim Gu was its police chief. His police guarded it and kept watch for spies.
lines.master: Kim Gu served as its police chief, and his police guarded it and kept watch for spies.

lines.rookie: Later, in 1940, Kim Gu became the head of that government.
lines.junior: Later, in 1940, Kim Gu became the leader of that government.
lines.master: Later, in 1940, Kim Gu rose to become the head of that government.
